title: U.S. House · Texas's 18th District
area: Central Houston and parts of Harris County.

context.text: Christian Menefee led the initial round of a special election on November 4, 2025 and won the special election runoff over Amanda Edwards on January 31, 2026, to fill the seat after Rep. Sylvester Turner died in March 2025. For the 2026 general election, Menefee defeated fellow incumbent U.S. Rep. Al Green in a May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff, 69.3% to 30.7%, after the two topped a crowded March 3, 2026 primary field. Ronald Whitfield defeated Elizabeth Vences, 55.1%-44.9%, in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary.

candidates.name: Christian Menefee
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2026); previously Harris County Attorney (2021–2025)

summary.text: Christian Menefee is the Democratic incumbent, a former commercial litigator who was elected Harris County Attorney in 2020 and won a special election to the seat in early 2026 after Rep. Sylvester Turner's death. He then defeated fellow incumbent Al Green in the May 2026 Democratic primary runoff. He serves on the Oversight and Government Reform and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

background.text: Grew up in Houston's public schools, the son of two U.S. Coast Guard veterans, and was the first in his family to graduate from college, according to his official biography; his Ballotpedia survey says he attended Klein Forest and Alief Hastings high schools.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2010 and a law degree from Washington University in St. Louis School of Law in 2013.

Practiced commercial litigation, beginning at Norton Rose Fulbright and later at Kirkland & Ellis LLP, according to his Ballotpedia survey; his official biography adds pro bono work advising the NAACP Legal Defense Fund and assisting immigrant families affected by the "Muslim ban" during President Trump's first term.

Won the November 3, 2020 general election for Harris County Attorney over John Nation and took office in 2021, succeeding Vince Ryan; was re-elected in November 2024 over Jacqueline Lucci Smith. His official biography says he was the youngest person and first Black attorney elected to the office.
As County Attorney, his official biography says his office brought lawsuits over health care funding, voting rights, and environmental pollution.

Led the first round of the November 4, 2025 special election for the seat left vacant by Rep. Sylvester Turner's death, won the January 31, 2026 runoff over Amanda Edwards, and was sworn in to the U.S. House in early February 2026.

Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and is a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and Congressional Black Caucus, among others.
Defeated fellow incumbent Al Green in the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff, 69.3% to 30.7%.
According to his official biography, he lives in Houston with his wife, Kaitlyn, an attorney, and their two sons.

record.text: Defeated incumbent U.S. Rep. Al Green in the May 26, 2026 Democratic primary runoff for this seat, 69.3% to 30.7%.

candidates.name: Ronald Whitfield
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary outright over Elizabeth Vences, 55.1% to 44.9%.

summary.text: Ronald Whitfield is the Republican nominee challenging Menefee in a heavily Democratic Houston-area district. He first appeared on the ballot as a Republican candidate in the November 2025 special election for the seat and won the March 2026 Republican primary. Little other biographical information is publicly available.

background.text: Ran as a Republican in the November 4, 2025 special election for Texas's 18th District, receiving 1.5% of the vote in a field of more than a dozen candidates.
Won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary for the district over Elizabeth Vences, 55.1% to 44.9%.
